reason: Selected methods and ablations support reader-dependent context budgets, fact-augmented indexing and qualified temporal filtering.

candidates.title: Tune retrieved-token budgets to the reader
candidates.rule: When building conversational memory, sweep the retrieved-token budget separately for each reader model instead of maximizing retrieved context by default.
candidates.passage: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct’s performance drops sharply beyond 3k retrieved tokens
candidates.finding: GPT-4o continues improving beyond 20k retrieved tokens, while Llama 3.1 8B degrades beyond 3k. Decomposing sessions into rounds helps GPT-4o more than the smaller reader.
candidates.conditions: Budget-aware comparison of memory value granularity; questions include extraction, multi-session and temporal reasoning, updates and abstention.
candidates.limitations: Historical models and constructed histories. The observed thresholds are setup-specific; they are not fixed limits for every workload or modern model.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep token budgets and memory granularity per reader on development tasks; freeze the configuration before measuring accuracy, abstention and latency on held-out histories.

candidates.title: Augment memory keys with facts while retaining original evidence
candidates.rule: For conversational-memory retrieval, compare indexing the original round plus extracted user facts with indexing only compressed facts; keep original text available to the reader.
candidates.passage: using these condensed forms alone does not enhance the memory recall performance.
candidates.finding: Round-level value-plus-fact keys improve recall@10 from 0.692 to 0.784. GPT-4o top-10 QA rises from 0.670 to 0.720. Summary-only or fact-only keys do not reliably improve retrieval; improvements vary by granularity and reader.
candidates.conditions: Document expansion concatenates facts with the original retrieval value. Comparisons include both rounds and whole sessions.
candidates.limitations: Fact extraction adds cost and can introduce errors. Session-level effects are mixed, including some QA regressions; this is not proof that all compression is harmful.
candidates.validation_test: Compare original-only, fact-only and original-plus-fact indexing using the same retriever and reader budget; measure retrieval recall, downstream QA and unsupported facts.

candidates.title: Validate time-range extraction before filtering memory
candidates.rule: For time-sensitive memory queries, test event-date indexing and query-derived time filters only with a model that can reliably infer the required date range.
candidates.passage: Llama 8B, on the other hand, struggles to generate accurate time ranges
candidates.finding: GPT-4o-derived time filters improve several retrieval measures, especially with fact-expanded keys; Llama 3.1 8B filters show mixed or negative effects. Some individual GPT-4o cells also decline, so the benefit is not uniform.
workloads: Temporal reasoning subset of LongMemEval M
candidates.conditions: Values carry event-date metadata and a model extracts a query time range to narrow retrieval.
candidates.limitations: Reported gains concern retrieval; they do not alone establish end-to-end QA improvement or safe hard filtering. Incorrect dates can discard decisive evidence.
candidates.validation_test: Measure date-range precision and evidence recall before enabling filters; compare filtered and unfiltered retrieval on ambiguous dates, relative time and updated facts.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
